item.description:
OrcaRouter Lite Launches as Self-Hosted AI Model Router with Managed Safety Net

OrcaRouter Lite, an open-source single-workspace edition of OrcaRouter, has been released as a self-hosted server that combines local control with a managed fallback for AI model routing. item.title: WhisperLiveKit: Self-Hosted, Real-Time Speech-to-Text Pipeline
item.description:
WhisperLiveKit: Self-Hosted, Real-Time Speech-to-Text Pipeline

WhisperLiveKit is a self-hosted, ultra-low-latency speech-to-text pipeline that provides real-time transcription, speaker diarization, and translation. It is designed to handle streaming audio efficiently while offering API compatibility with major platforms.

🔍 Overview

The system supports real-time, local speech-to-text with streaming Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), speaker diarization, and translation. It is built to process audio as it is being spoken rather than waiting for complete utterances.

🧩 How it works

WhisperLiveKit utilizes state-of-the-art simultaneous speech research for intelligent buffering and incremental processing. Simple Whisper models are not ideal for this use case because they are designed for complete utterances; processing small segments loses context and cuts off words mid-syllable, resulting in poor transcription.

The pipeline integrates several advanced components:

  • Simul-Whisper/Streaming: SOTA 2025 ultra-low latency transcription using the AlignAtt policy.
  • WhisperStreaming: Low latency transcription using the LocalAgreement policy (SOTA 2023).
  • Streaming Sortformer: Advanced real-time speaker diarization (SOTA 2025).
  • NLLW: Simultaneous translation from and to 200 languages based on distilled NLLB models.
  • Qwen3-ASR-causal: Causal streaming audio encoder where each audio block is encoded exactly once with constant compute per audio second.
  • AlignAtt4LLM: Simultaneous translation with decoder-only LLMs featuring attention-gated commits and append-only output.

⚙️ Key details

  • Architecture: The backend supports multiple concurrent users and includes Voice Activity Detection to reduce overhead when no voice is detected.
  • APIs: Provides OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and Deepgram-compatible WebSocket interfaces.
  • Streaming: Native WebSocket support is available for real-time streaming.
  • Language Support: Check the specific tokenizer documentation for the list of all available languages.
  • Troubleshooting: A troubleshooting guide is available for step-by-step fixes collected from recent GPU issues.

🚀 Availability

WhisperLiveKit is available for installation and local execution via command-line tools.

  • Installation: pip install whisperlivekit
  • Server Execution:
    • wlk --model base --language en (Starts server at http://localhost:8000)
    • wlk run whisper:tiny (Auto-pulls model and starts server)
  • File Transcription:
    • wlk transcribe meeting.wav
    • wlk transcribe --format srt podcast.mp3 -o podcast.srt (Generates subtitles)
  • Model Management:
    • wlk models (View installed models)
    • wlk pull large-v3 (Download a model)
    • wlk rm large-v3 (Delete a model)
  • Benchmarking: wlk bench (Test speed and accuracy)
  • API Access:
    • REST: curl http://localhost:8000/v1/audio/transcriptions -F file=@audio.wav
    • SDK: Compatible with OpenAI Python SDK (client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="unused"))
    • WebSocket: ws://localhost:8000/asr

#WhisperLiveKit #SpeechToText #RealTimeAI #SelfHosted #Translation

Source: QuentinFuxa/WhisperLiveKit

item.title: Gitea Enables Self-Hosted Software Development Across All Go Platforms
item.description:
Gitea Enables Self-Hosted Software Development Across All Go Platforms

Gitea is a self-hosted all-in-one software development service designed to be the easiest, fastest, and most painless way to set up development infrastructure. It integrates Git hosting, code management, and team collaboration into a single platform.

🧩 How it works

Gitea is written in the Go programming language, which allows it to run across all platforms and architectures supported by Go. This includes:

  • Operating Systems: Linux, macOS, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, and Windows.
  • Architectures: x86, amd64, ARM, RISC-V 64, and PowerPC.

The system supports a comprehensive set of development tools, including:

  • Git hosting and code management
  • Code review and issue tracking
  • Project kanban and wiki functionality
  • Team collaboration
  • Package registry and CI/CD (which can reuse GitHub Actions)

⚙️ Key details

The project provides extensive documentation covering installation, administration, usage, and development. Key resources and commands include:

Resource Purpose
./gitea web Starts the server after building from source
./gitea help Displays all available commands
docs/build-source.md Instructions for building from source or creating distribution packages
docs/development.md Guides for setting up local environments, linting, and testing

For developers contributing to the project, the expected workflow is Fork → Patch → Push → Pull Request. Security vulnerabilities must be reported privately to security@gitea.io.

🚀 Availability

Users can access Gitea through several methods:

  • Online Demonstration: demo.gitea.com
  • Free Service: gitea.com offers a free service with a limited number of repositories.
  • Cloud Deployment: A free trial is available at cloud.gitea.com.
  • Container Deployment: The official image is available for Docker, Podman, or other container runtimes on your own server.
  • Community Support: Questions can be directed to the Discord server or the Discourse forum.

The ecosystem includes an official Go SDK, a CLI tool called gt, and an action runner for Gitea Actions. Third-party projects, SDKs, plugins, and themes are listed on the gitea/awesome-gitea repository.

#Gitea #SelfHosted #DevOps #Git #CI/CD #OpenSource

Source: go-gitea/gitea

item.title: Locally.Uncensored 3.0.10 Adds Cross-Platform AI Support and Computer Control
item.description:
Locally.Uncensored 3.0.10 Adds Cross-Platform AI Support and Computer Control

🔍 Overview

Locally.Uncensored has released version 3.0.10, providing an all-in-one local AI studio for desktop environments. The application enables users to run chat, image generation, video generation, and coding agents directly on their own hardware without requiring Docker, terminal configurations, or cloud connectivity.

🧩 How it works

The software operates as a locally hosted web server featuring a React UI. It includes a “Unified Canvas” for generation tasks such as in-painting, out-painting, and brush tool support. Users manage their AI workflows through a node-based architecture or an organized gallery system for storing and remixing content.

⚙️ Key details

  • Model Support: Compatible with SD 1.5, 2.0, SDXL, SD 3.5 (Medium and Large), Flux.1 Dev, and Flux.2 Dev, as well as support for ckpt, diffusers, and certain gguf models.
  • Agent Capabilities: Includes a coding agent for development tasks.
  • Security: Built via GitHub Actions from public source code; Windows installers are code-signed via SignPath.io.

🚀 Availability

Locally.Uncensored 3.0.10 is available for the following platforms:

Platform Supported Formats
Windows 10/11 NSIS installer (.exe), .msi
Linux .AppImage, .deb, .rpm
macOS (Apple Silicon) .dmg (Beta)
Android 7.0+ .apk

Note: Intel Macs are not supported. Features like computer control are currently under testing for macOS.

#LocalAI #OpenSource #GenAI #SelfHosted

Source: vstorm-co/agenticos Source: lidge-jun/opencodex Source: Shubhamsaboo/awesome-llm-apps Source: invoke-ai/InvokeAI Source: PurpleDoubleD/locally-uncensored

item.title: Local AI Agent Hermes Enables Personal Automation on High‑Memory Macs
item.description:
Local AI Agent Hermes Enables Personal Automation on High‑Memory Macs

I’m embarking on a journey I’ve so far been hesitant to go on: actually using AI on the regular, this time by running a self‑hosted agent locally on a powerful Mac.

🔍 Overview

  • Concerns about giving personal data to cloud services motivated a shift to local AI.
  • Apple’s new Mac desktops are marketed for local AI workloads, and upcoming RTX Spark Windows machines promise up to 128 GB RAM for agentic AI.
  • The author’s M5 Ultra Mac Studio has 256 GB unified memory, sufficient for almost any model.

🛠️ How it works

  • Hermes is a self‑hosted AI agent desktop app that runs on macOS, Windows, and Linux.
  • It is completely free when using local LLMs.
  • The onboarding interface includes a model picker; the author selected Qwen 3.8 Flash Next, a 125‑billion‑parameter model (~105 GB).
  • Hermes can be controlled via a Telegram bot, enabling daily briefings and other tasks.

📦 Devices & Models

Device Memory / Specs Planned Use
M5 Ultra Mac Studio 256 GB unified memory Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next and other large models
M6 Mac Mini – Try smaller Qwen models
M5 MacBook Air – Try smaller Qwen models
Asus TUF Gaming A14 (AMD Strix Halo) – Try smaller Qwen models
RTX Spark (future) up to 128 GB RAM Agentic AI experiments

✅ Practical Use Cases

  • Daily morning briefing: Hermes scans email and calendar, reports urgent items and weather; set up as a cron job at 7:30 am (macOS must be awake).
  • Steam library organization: After registering a Steam Web API key, Hermes categorized over 400 games in minutes; the key was revoked afterward.
  • Financial record crunching: Hermes processed sensitive financial data locally.
  • Spec‑comparison spreadsheet: Generated a laptop comparison sheet for a new, embargoed device, keeping the information on‑device.
  • Benchmark automation: Working on a script to run repeated laptop benchmark tests, reducing manual effort.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Local AI requires explicit permissions (e.g., Steam API key) that can be revoked after use.
  • Running models locally eliminates token costs; the author chose a large model to start.
  • Larger models (billions of parameters) generally outperform smaller ones.
  • The daily briefing initially failed until the author ensured the Mac was not asleep when the cron job fired.

💡 Why it matters

  • Sensitive data stays on the user’s machine, addressing privacy concerns with cloud services.
  • Free, local execution of powerful LLMs makes advanced AI capabilities accessible without recurring token fees.
  • A single self‑hosted app can automate a range of personal productivity tasks, from email summaries to game library management.

#LocalAI #Hermes #SelfHosted #LLM #Automation

Source: Learning to use local AI is exciting, overwhelming, and frustrating

item.title: Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents
item.description:
Codex Pooler Introduced as Self-Hosted Gateway for Codex-Compatible Agents

Codex Pooler is a self-hosted gateway designed to run Codex-compatible agents, tools, and automation using stable Pool API keys.

🔍 Overview

Codex Pooler allows operators to manage pools, accounts, API keys, saved resets, routing, request accounting, audit logs, and health. The system is designed so that operators do not store raw Codex secrets, bearer tokens, prompts, files, audio, or images.

🧩 How it works

Clients send OpenAI-compatible or Codex backend requests to the Codex Pooler. The system then selects an eligible account based on the following criteria:

  • Model support
  • Quota evidence
  • Limits
  • Session continuity
  • Routing policy
  • Health

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Stable Pool API keys Provides clients with one credential regardless of whether the Pool has one or several upstream accounts, avoiding the distribution of raw Codex account material.
Eligibility-aware routing Routes requests to accounts with matching health, session state, Pool policy, usable quota evidence, and compatible model support.
Codex backend compatibility Allows Codex-compatible clients to point at Codex Pooler while maintaining usage, compacting, and responses.

💡 Why it matters

  • Credential Isolation: It works with one upstream Codex account for client normalization, metadata-only operations, saved reset visibility, and credential isolation.
  • Scalability: Additional accounts can be added for routing and shared capacity across eligible accounts.
  • Stability: The Pool key remains stable even when capacity, reset policy, lifecycle state, and upstream assignments change.
  • Administrative Control: Instance owners maintain the global administration surface, while instance admins are restricted to their assigned Pools.

#Codex #API #AIagents #SelfHosted

Source: icoretech/codex-pooler

item.title: Pizza Bot Released as an Open Source, Self-Hosted AI Agent Application
item.description:
Pizza Bot Released as an Open Source, Self-Hosted AI Agent Application

Today marks the release of Pizza Bot, an open source application that runs AI agents in the background and provides them with an inbox interface. Designed to keep agents working without constant human monitoring, Pizza Bot ensures that background agents return to you only when they are finished or when they get stuck, rather than before.

🔍 Overview

Pizza Bot is a finished application built for people who need daily work done rather than for writing software. The tool originally began inside Amazon, where more than 2,000 employees utilized earlier versions for various tasks, including:

  • Meeting preparation and follow-ups
  • Email drafting
  • Slack summaries
  • CRM logging
  • Day prioritization
  • Web research

A small team rebuilt the application from the ground up as an open source project, a process made practical through the use of coding agents.

🧩 How It Works

Pizza Bot operates on an inbox model to manage background tasks. Users can initiate a task manually, set it on a schedule, or allow a webhook to start it. The interface organizes tasks using specific folders and panels:

Folder / Panel Description
Unread Completed work that you have not yet reviewed.
Action Paused work waiting on your approval or your answer.
Activity Shows work the main agent handed to a specialist, including that specialist’s own transcript.

To expand capabilities, Pizza Bot connects to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers for tools, and it works with Agent Skills, which is the Markdown convention introduced by Anthropic for packaging specialist knowledge.

⚙️ Key Details

Pizza Bot is structured as both a server and a client:

  • The Server: Runs the agent, owns its state, and answers over HTTP.
  • The Client: Can be the Electron desktop application, a web browser, or a terminal.

The desktop application wraps both components, starting its own local server and connecting to it. Because the agent’s work lives on the server, a run keeps going when you close the thread, reload the page, or switch devices. A client that reconnects will catch up on what it missed.

If you host the server on an always-on machine or inside a container, you can access the same threads from a laptop, phone, or terminal. Conversely, quitting the desktop application stops its local server and ends its current runs. However, because runs are checkpointed as they go, you only lose the step currently in flight rather than the entire thread.

🛡️ Security and Compatibility

Pizza Bot is self-hosted, features no telemetry, and runs locally. Everything it stores remains in a folder you own, and the application only listens on your own machine unless you configure it otherwise. Nothing leaves your machine unless you explicitly send it there.

It allows you to choose your own model provider, with support for:

  • Anthropic
  • Amazon Bedrock
  • Google Gemini
  • OpenAI
  • OpenRouter
  • Local models through Ollama

#PizzaBot #AIAgents #OpenSource #SelfHosted

Source: Introducing Pizza Bot, an open source inbox for AI agents that work in the background | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Codex Pooler launches as a self-hosted gateway for Codex-compatible agents
item.description:
Codex Pooler launches as a self-hosted gateway for Codex-compatible agents

Codex Pooler has been introduced as a self-hosted gateway designed for running Codex-compatible agents, tools, and automation through stable Pool API keys.

🔍 Overview

Codex Pooler connects clients to upstream accounts while maintaining a stable access key interface. The gateway supports different configurations depending on the number of accounts:

  • Single upstream Codex account: Provides credential isolation, client normalization, metadata-only operations, and saved reset visibility.
  • Multiple upstream accounts: Added to provide shared capacity and routing across eligible accounts.

🧩 How it works

Clients send familiar Codex backend or OpenAI-compatible requests to the gateway. While upstream assignments, lifecycle states, reset policies, and capacity change behind the scenes, the external Pool key remains stable.

When a request is made, Codex Pooler selects an eligible account based on the following criteria:

  • Model support
  • Quota evidence
  • Limits
  • Session continuity
  • Routing policy
  • Health

⚙️ Key details

Operators and administrators are provided with specific control surfaces to manage their environments securely.

Administration Roles

  • Instance owners: Maintain the global administration surface.
  • Instance admins: Work exclusively with their assigned Pools.

Operator Management

Operators get a single centralized place to manage Pools, accounts, API keys, saved resets, routing, request accounting, audit logs, and health. This management is conducted without storing:

  • Prompts
  • Files
  • Audio
  • Images
  • Bearer tokens
  • Raw Codex secrets

#CodexPooler #DeveloperTools #AIInfrastructure #SelfHosted

Source: icoretech/codex-pooler
